bullets.text: In and out in minutes, not rushed

sections.name: What Section
sections.title: If your headaches start at the base of your skull

paras.t: Some headaches start at the back of the head and wrap forward. Some sit behind the eyes by mid-afternoon. Some come with a stiff neck and tight shoulders every single time.
If yours follow long days at a desk, get worse when your neck is tight, or never really go away, there's a good chance your neck is part of the problem.
Tension headaches feel like a band or pressure around the head. They usually come with tight neck and shoulder muscles.
Headaches from the neck start when the joints and muscles at the top of the neck refer pain up into the head. They often get worse with certain neck positions, like looking down at a laptop.
Migraines are their own thing, with more triggers than just the neck. They have their own page.

callouts.title: Dr. Morgan treats the neck part.
callouts.text: When your exam shows your headaches are coming from the neck and upper back, that's what he works on. When they're not, he'll tell you.

sections.title: Find it, fix it, keep it from coming back

bullets.body: A full history of your headaches (when, where, how often, what sets them off) and an exam of your neck and upper back. Digital X-rays if your exam calls for them.
Chiropractic adjustments to the neck and upper back. Dr. Morgan starts gentle, especially on the first visit.
Once the problem is corrected, most patients move to maintenance, about once every two weeks.

sections.name: First Visit Section
sections.title: Your first visit, start to finish

paras.t: First visit runs about 30 minutes. After that, most visits take a few minutes. Dr. Morgan built the practice around working people.

steps.title: We find out what is actually happening
steps.text: Full history and exam. What hurts, what you have already tried, what you want to get back to doing. Any necessary digital X-rays, taken on site.

steps.title: Dr. Morgan shows you the imaging, same day
steps.text: He marks it up and walks you through it right there. You will see what he sees. Most patients get their first adjustment the same visit.

steps.title: You come back for the full report
steps.text: Within a few days, Dr. Morgan lays out what he found and exactly what he recommends. What it will take, how long, and what it costs. Then you decide.

sections.name: What Section
sections.title: How long until this actually feels better

paras.t: Most people want a number before they start. Dr. Morgan will give you one, just not before he has examined you and looked at your imaging. He will not guess.
What he can tell you up front is how it usually goes, including the part most offices skip: the first two weeks are uneven.
If you are only trying to get out of pain, a shorter plan can do that. If you want it to stay fixed, it takes about 90 days. Dr. Morgan will give you both options and let you pick.

tags.text: Inconsistent, and that's normal. You'll have a good day and think it's fixed, then a bad one and think it's not working. Dr. Morgan warns you about this on day one. Real change usually starts around the end of week two, and better sleep is often the first thing people notice.

The bulk of the plan. A typical plan is about 24 visits over 90 days, two to three times a week at the start, then less often as you improve. Some people need fewer. Dr. Morgan checks your progress along the way.
Most patients move to maintenance, about once every two weeks. Some stop entirely. Dr. Morgan will tell you when you're there.

faqs.a: When they're coming from the neck and upper back, often yes. The exam tells Dr. Morgan whether that's what's going on. If it's not, he'll tell you.

faqs.q: How do I know if my headache is coming from my neck?
faqs.a: Common signs: it starts at the base of the skull, it gets worse with certain neck positions, and it comes with a stiff neck or tight shoulders. The exam confirms it.
Only if your exam calls for it. If Dr. Morgan takes them, they happen on site at your first visit.

faqs.q: How many visits will I need?
faqs.a: Dr. Morgan won't know until he's examined you. A typical plan is about 24 visits over 90 days, two to three times a week at the start.

faqs.q: When should I go to the ER instead?
faqs.a: If it's the worst headache of your life, it came on suddenly, or it comes with confusion, weakness, trouble speaking, a stiff neck with fever, or follows a hit to the head, go to an emergency room.
